Jamaat-e-Islami and the Question of Knowledge and Research: Where Are the Think Tanks?

Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami is one of the country’s major Islamist political organisations. Representing a significant segment of the population, the party currently serves as the opposition in the national parliament. Its organisational discipline, capable cadre base, and extensive political experience have established it as an important force in Bangladesh’s political landscape.

However, for an ideologically driven Islamic movement, organisational strength alone is not sufficient. A strong intellectual culture, original research, policy analysis, and the capacity to address contemporary intellectual challenges are equally indispensable.

Islamic history shows that movements which have exerted a lasting positive influence on society have not relied solely on organisational activities. Rather, they have advanced research, education, publishing, and the development of ideas alongside their organisational efforts.

Research, therefore, is not an ancillary concern for an Islamic organisation; it is one of the principal foundations of its intellectual leadership, policy maturity, and future development.

Viewed from this perspective, the research infrastructure of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami does not yet appear to have developed to the expected level. In particular, there is no clearly visible, robust, professional, and internationally competitive academic research institution dedicated to sustained original research on Islamic thought, governance, economics, sociology, law, education, culture, and contemporary global issues.

In my observation, the Bangladesh Islamic Centre appears to have undertaken some research initiatives in the past. At present, however, its activities seem to focus more on conventional publishing and routine organisational work than on the systematic production of research-based knowledge.

In my assessment, the current activities do not sufficiently demonstrate the fundamental components of institutional research to the extent one would expect. These include planned research projects, evidence-based analysis, peer-reviewed publications, policy-oriented research, and internationally recognised academic output. Consequently, its current activities do not appear to meet the expected standards of institutional research.

Similarly, although an institution called the Maulana Maududi Research Academy exists, sustained research, reference works, and policy-oriented publications capable of making a significant impact on contemporary national and international academic discourse are not yet sufficiently evident—at least, this is how the situation appears from my personal observation.

A similar situation can be observed in the field of publishing.

Although publishing houses associated with the party have made certain contributions, their output at present appears, in most cases, to remain confined to conventional book publishing. High-quality original research, policy papers, research reports, academic journals, think-tank publications, and internationally competitive translation projects addressing contemporary social, political, economic, technological, and intellectual questions remain relatively limited.

It is worth acknowledging, however, that several privately owned publishing houses associated with the Jamaat-e-Islami milieu have published valuable translations and important books in response to the needs of modern readers. These initiatives deserve recognition as positive contributions. Nevertheless, owing to the inherent limitations of commercial enterprises, they are not always in a position to undertake costly, long-term, and institutionally organised research.

On the other hand, there are many qualified ʿUlama, accomplished researchers, university teachers, and specialists in various fields, both at home and abroad, who are directly or indirectly associated with the Jamaat-e-Islami tradition. Yet Jamaat has not been able to harness their knowledge, expertise, and research experience over the long term within a well-organised institutional research framework. Although some initiatives of this kind may exist in particular areas, their tangible outcomes remain less visible than might be expected.

Several practical factors may contribute to this situation, including the absence of suitable institutional platforms, limitations in effective coordination, inadequate research funding and institutional support, difficulties in properly recognising and engaging specialists according to their expertise, and their personal and professional commitments.

As a result, this substantial pool of intellectual talent is not being fully utilised for knowledge production, policy-oriented research, addressing contemporary intellectual challenges, and the long-term development of the organisation’s policies and strategic thinking.

In the contemporary world, political competition is no longer confined to securing public support; it is also a competition in knowledge, research, policy innovation, and intellectual leadership.

Consequently, if an Islamic movement fails to invest consistently in research, academic excellence, and the development of ideas, it will become increasingly difficult for it to provide effective responses to contemporary religious, social, political, and philosophical questions, cultivate policy leadership, and sustain its long-term influence.

Therefore, building a robust research infrastructure, establishing internationally recognised research institutions, creating an environment conducive to developing competent researchers, and investing in original knowledge production should be regarded as major strategic priorities for the future of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami.
